Chloe wants to paint a steel box that has the form of a rectangular prism. Two of the polygonal faces are $4\,\text{ft}\times 4\,\text{ft}$ squares. If the cost to paint the surface is $$6.50$ per square foot, how much will it cost her in total? Note that Chloe does *not* need to paint the square sides.

The net of our prism is the following.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930500/assets/7b84a48933abb96f605476c6d703406227b0fe5301b1457a447cdbb3f58f0937.png)

 

$$

$$

Each side face (apart from the square faces) of our solid is a rectangle, where the base is $7\,\text{ft}$ and the height is $4\,\text{ft}.$ Therefore

$$
\text{Area of the rectangle}=7\times 4=28\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.
$$

Now, the total area of the side surfaces consists of $4$ rectangular faces. 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area of the sides} & =4\times (\text{Area of the rectangle}) \\  & =4\times 28 \\  & =112\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the cost to paint the surface is $$6.50$ per square foot, the total amount that Chloe will have to pay is

$$
112\times 6.50=$728.
$$
